explanations: The OZ statute targets low-income community (LIC) tracts by eligibility rule; selected tracts having higher poverty than the general eligible pool is the statutorily intended outcome.

Governors chose which eligible tracts to nominate from an already poverty-skewed pool; higher poverty among selected-vs-unselected-eligible tracts may reflect a preference for nominating the most distressed eligible tracts.

Given the documented poverty/racial-composition correlation in U.S. census geography, a higher non-White share among poverty-selected tracts can follow mechanically from the poverty-selection criterion, without race being a direct selection factor.
competing_explanations.forbidden_inference_note: Retrieval contains no data linking the demographic selection pattern to investor behavior, fund positioning, contributions, or favoritism. c5 supports only a descriptive statistical comparison. It must not be read as evidence of deliberate racial targeting, investor self-dealing, or misconduct.

coverage_prose: This run establishes the statutory and administrative timeline of Opportunity Zone designation (TCJA 2017 authorization, gubernatorial nomination, Treasury certification, April/June 2018 announcements) plus the headline findings of one GAO oversight report, resting on 9 distinct sources after deduplication. It leaves the tract-count denominator unresolved (8,761 vs 8,764) and never reaches fund-formation dates, pre-designation land ownership, or SEC Form D filings. The central value-capture question — whether private capital was positioned in eventually-designated tracts before designation — remains entirely open and requires a further, targeted retrieval pass.
